payload.title: Engagement Ring Insurance and How to Get It
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s, affluent, interested in a destination wedding and other luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian in their 30s who has just bought (or is about to buy) an engagement ring worth more than anything else they carry, may be planning to propose overseas, and now wants to know, in plain words, which kinds of cover exist, what to check in a policy before relying on it, what paperwork to keep, and whether the ring is protected on the flight to a wedding abroad, without being sold a policy.
payload.goal: Click through to the destinations hub to start picturing where the wedding could happen (Wedded Concierge at /wonderland-concierge as the secondary CTA, placed in the travelling-to-a-destination-wedding section).
payload.angle: Page-one results are mostly insurer and jeweller sales pages pushing their own policy or quoting premium rules of thumb. This guide sells nothing and names no insurer: it is a neutral, Australia-specific checklist built only on public sources (ASIC Moneysmart, Understand Insurance from the Insurance Council of Australia, the General Insurance Code of Practice, AFCA, Smartraveller, Jewellers Association of Australia), and it follows the ring's real journey for a destination couple: the day of purchase, a proposal abroad before the ring is listed on any policy, the flight to the wedding, the week on the ground with pools, beaches and boats, and what to do (including the AFCA route) if a claim goes wrong.
must_include: Intro (60 to 120 words) answering the real question: an engagement ring is usually covered only if you set the cover up and read the conditions, and travel is where the gaps show.
Exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways (no prices, no insurer names).

Compliance line, once, near the top and again in the close: 'This is general information, not financial advice. Read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) and Target Market Determination (TMD) before you buy.' Explain PDS and TMD in plain words the first time. Source facts to verify: ASIC Moneysmart on reading the PDS; ASIC on what a TMD is.

Section: the three ways to insure a ring. (a) Home contents policy: specified or listed items versus blanket or unspecified cover, and why a single item limit can sit below the ring's value; (b) standalone jewellery policy; (c) travel insurance, which typically caps valuables per item and is not a substitute. Facts to source: Understand Insurance (ICA) and ASIC Moneysmart explanations of specified vs unspecified items and item limits; Smartraveller and Moneysmart on travel insurance limits and exclusions for valuables. Describe limits generically; no figures.

Section: policy checks, as a scannable checklist or table: loss vs theft vs accidental damage (including a lost stone); overseas or worldwide cover and any time limit away from home; agreed value vs market value vs replacement value; replace (often through the insurer's chosen supplier) vs cash settlement; excess (that one exists, no amounts); conditions such as unattended items, carry-on vs checked luggage, safe or locked storage, and duty to disclose or update the value; when cover starts. Facts to source: Understand Insurance glossary (agreed value, market value, excess); General Insurance Code of Practice for what insurers must tell you; anything not supported becomes 'check your policy' wording.

Section: valuations and paperwork. Keep the receipt, grading report (link diamond-buying-guide for GIA/IGI reports), an independent valuation, clear photos from several angles, and a note of any laser inscription. Facts to source: Jewellers Association of Australia on valuations and the revaluation interval (sister posts cite a two-year revaluation; reuse the same fact and source); what a valuation for insurance purposes is versus a sale price.

Section: lab-grown versus natural. Valuation and replacement are assessed on what the stone is, so disclosure on the report and valuation must be correct; link /style-advice/lab-grown-diamonds. Source: JAA or report-issuer wording only; no resale or price claims.

Section: insure it from the day you buy it, including when you propose abroad. The gap between collecting the ring and listing it on a policy; telling the insurer about overseas travel before the proposal trip; carry-on only. Link the proposal guides (/proposal/how-to-propose-a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-perfect-moment, /the-top-proposal-destinations-in-italy). Facts to source: Smartraveller on travel insurance and valuables; policy-dependent points worded as 'check your policy'.

Section: travelling to your destination wedding. Engagement ring plus wedding bands in the carry-on, tell your insurer your travel dates, safes and unattended-item conditions, local police report if stolen (Smartraveller), swap to a plain band for water and boat days (link engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle). This is where a Wedded Advisor's role in planning the travel naturally comes up (Concierge secondary CTA, claims only from brand-facts.md).

Section: making a claim and if it goes wrong. What to gather (report, receipts, valuation, photos), internal dispute resolution first, then AFCA as the free, independent external dispute scheme. Facts to source: General Insurance Code of Practice (claims timeframes and complaints handling, quote only what the Code states); AFCA on eligibility and that it is free to consumers; Moneysmart on complaints.

FAQ (3 to 6), e.g. Is my engagement ring covered by home contents insurance? Does travel insurance cover my engagement ring overseas? How often should I get my ring revalued? Should I insure the ring before I propose? What is the difference between agreed value and market value?
Close inviting the next step (destinations hub), with the Wedded Advisor as the person who plans travel for the wedding, using only brand-facts.md claims.

Internal links: /expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring (ring budget), /style-advice/diamond-buying-guide, /style-advice/lab-grown-diamonds, /style-advice/engagement-ring-setting-for-active-lifestyle, /style-advice/engagement-ring-styles, proposal guides, /wonderland-concierge, /destinations. Drafts publish together; note backlinks needed from the settings and styles posts' short insurance sections to this full guide.
avoid: Naming any insurer, broker, comparison site or jeweller, or describing a specific product.
Any premium, excess amount, sum insured, item limit figure or 'costs about X% of the ring's value' rule of thumb.
Recommending a policy, a type of cover as 'best', or telling the reader what to buy (general information only; no personal advice wording such as 'you should get').
Stating what 'most policies' cover unless a cited regulator or industry source says it; otherwise 'check your policy'.
Legal or tax claims, resale value claims, and any claim about lab-grown vs natural prices.
Fear-led copy or stacked worst-case stories; calm, precise tone per voice guide.
Repeating the settings and styles posts' care advice at length; link to them instead.
Any Wedded Wonderland claim not in brand-facts.md (business details are deferred); competitor branding or copy; em dashes; US spelling.
